source.title: Detection Accuracy for Evaluating Compositional Explanations of Units
source.authors: Sayo M. Makinwa; Biagio La Rosa; R. Capobianco

record.tranche_reason: The study applies concept-based explanations to units in image classifiers and explicitly reports polysemantic units, but does not use the original claim’s example or method.
record.gate_note: The study reports comparisons of IoU and Detection Accuracy, explanation-length results, and correlations with model prediction accuracy. Those outcomes assess explanation scoring and quality, not directly whether units respond to unrelated inputs, so they are not included as rows. The one row records the study’s explicit qualitative statement that polysemantic units occur among units receiving longer explanations.
record.test_reason: The study proposes Detection Accuracy for scoring and stopping compositional explanations of final-layer CNN units. Its only mention of polysemanticity is one clause: units with explanations longer than 1 behave as Mu and Andreas noted, including being polysemantic, with Figure 6(B) examples. It gives no count, share, criterion or analysis of polysemantic units. It does not separate unrelated from related concept mixtures. That passing remark repeats a prior finding and does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that Detection Accuracy evaluates explanations of different lengths more objectively and correlates better with model prediction accuracy. It can replace the maximum-length hyper-parameter as a stopping criterion and exposes specialized units whose length-1 explanations abstract their longer ones. It is more valuable as an evaluation metric than as an optimization metric.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Network Dissection and compositional concept explanations with a proposed Detection Accuracy metric; it does not reproduce the original sources’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Explanation evaluations vary with the scoring metric (IoU versus Detection Accuracy) and explanation length; the study does not show that these choices change polysemantic classifications.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet-18, the scoring metric changes explanation length. With Detection Accuracy as stopping criterion, 245 of 512 units get length-1 explanations instead of fixed length-3 compositions. 179 of these (~73%) are single concepts that abstract their longer IoU-based explanations. IoU rates compositional explanations higher for ~100% of units; Detection Accuracy does so for ~43–61%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How unit explanations are scored (IoU vs Detection Accuracy) changes how many units receive multi-concept explanations. This could change apparent polysemanticity rates, but the study does not measure polysemanticity directly.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference of the Italian Association for Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The only direct polysemanticity finding is qualitative and unquantified. The study does not report specific unrelated inputs for the units or estimate the prevalence of polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No direct polysemanticity outcome beyond r1. Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–4 report explanation scores, explanation lengths, and correlations with prediction accuracy, rather than polysemanticity measurements.

untested.parts: Whether image-classifier units respond to unrelated inputs, with examples or prevalence; InceptionV1 is not studied.
Architecture, activation or regularization effects on polysemanticity share. Four CNNs are used, but polysemanticity is not compared across them.
Whether mixtures reflect a shared feature. The 'perceptual abstraction' units are related, but this is not framed or counted against polysemanticity.
The study shows explanation length depends on the scoring metric. It never counts how many units are judged polysemantic under each metric.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with a V1 'supports' label rests on a single unquantified clause that defers to Mu and Andreas [23]; I downgrade it to 'discusses'. The Section 4.3 and Table 1 results on metric-dependent explanation length are adjacent to V7. They are recorded under fits_no_version because polysemantic classification is never measured.

versions.untested_parts: No InceptionV1 or neuron 4e:55; no specific unrelated input examples or prevalence estimate.
Transformer language models and token/context polysemanticity.
Superposition and capacity pressure as a cause.
Initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes without capacity pressure.
Changes in polysemanticity prevalence by architecture, activation function, or regularization, and performance costs.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons share a feature or related job, and how often genuinely unrelated mixtures occur.
The study compares explanation scores and lengths, but does not measure whether those choices change which units are classified as polysemantic or examine different activation ranges.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.stage_stated: trained on the Places365 dataset; stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Manual inspection of units assigned explanations by compositional search using Detection Accuracy as the stopping criterion.

conditions.value: compositional explanations; Detection Accuracy stopping criterion

rows.measure: Reported types of unit behavior associated with explanations
rows.value: Units with explanation lengths greater than 1 may have lexically coherent or incoherent perceptual abstractions, or be polysemantic.
rows.note: Qualitative statement only; the study gives no count or share of polysemantic units in this group.
rows.check: This is a qualitative restatement that units behave as in Mu and Andreas [23], not a measurement. It has no polysemanticity criterion, no count, and no demonstration that the mixed concepts are unrelated. 'Observed' overstates it; it cannot support V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-18 final-layer units with explanation lengths greater than 1 under the Detection Accuracy stopping setup
reader_labels.reason: The authors explicitly include polysemantic units among the reported behaviors in this setting (r1); they do not quantify their prevalence or provide particular mixed-input examples.
